subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: refcount the weighted interleave state instead of copying it

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about potential cache fighting and suggested exploring SRCU for better performance. Also mentioned that backporting beyond 6.18 would be prevented by updating to the new fast srcu mechanism.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sun, Aug 23, 2026 at 11:52:55PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> On Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 04:06:03AM +0100, Matthew Wilcox wrote:
> > On Sun, Aug 23, 2026 at 10:41:17PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> > 
> > Bit of a shame to take/put a refcount on every memory allocation.  That
> > seems like it might hurt (even being on a different cacheline).  Would
> > it make more sense to use SRCU for this?
> 
> Bulk allocation - from some measurements it's about once per 100-pages
> on average.  Looking back at the data I was getting about 41 refs per
> 4096 pages (16MB chunks).
> 
> Have to imagine there's other cache fighting in that stack too. 
> 
> I'm less familiar with the rules around SRCU so i shied away from it,
> but I will take a look.
> 

I will update to the new fast srcu mechanism, but it'll prevent
backporting beyond 6.18.

Best to backport the gfp fix and update to srcu in normal cadence.

Will submit separately.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Decided to update the patch to use the new fast srcu mechanism, but noted that it would prevent backporting beyond 6.18 and suggested submitting a separate patch for the gfp fix.

2026-08-24.patch_summary: The patch proposes to refcount the weighted interleave state instead of copying it, which could potentially reduce memory allocation overhead.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that the patch may not be optimal for bulk allocation scenarios, but is less familiar with SRCU and plans to investigate further.
reviews.raw_body:
Bulk allocation - from some measurements it's about once per 100-pages
on average.  Looking back at the data I was getting about 41 refs per
4096 pages (16MB chunks).

Have to imagine there's other cache fighting in that stack too. 

I'm less familiar with the rules around SRCU so i shied away from it,
but I will take a look.

~Gregory

2026-08-23.patch_summary: This patch refactors the handling of the weighted interleave state in the Linux kernel's memory policy module. Instead of copying the state on every access, it introduces a reference counting mechanism to manage the state's lifetime. This change reduces memory allocation and deallocation overhead, fixes a bug related to GFP_KERNEL and partial allocations, and ensures that the state is properly cleaned up even in the presence of concurrent accesses.
